startup.name: Uno Wallet
startup.one_liner: The AI mobile wallet that replaces Apple Pay
startup.description: Consumer mobile wallet with AI that aims to replace Apple Pay as the way people pay. Two founders in San Francisco; the input gives no product details, traction or business model beyond the claim.

yc_acceptance.basis: The input file places this company in the Spring 2026 batch, so acceptance is already known and this figure is reported for completeness only. The starting prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md, 0.6 to 2 percent third party range); the near certainty comes from the stated batch, not from a model of the company.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC is already past, so the only residual risk is a data error in the input about batch membership. Had the company been an ordinary applicant, the most plausible rejection reason would be: A claim to replace Apple Pay with no stated distribution, regulatory plan or traction, from two founders in a space where the platform owner controls access.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --industry B2B --years 2022-2024: seed known-only 61% (lower 50%, upper 68%), cond 61% (n=88). Median months to seed 9 (p25 4, p75 19); time_to_milestones.csv era 2022+ p75 is 14 months.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 7 months from the as_of date to 2026-11-17. The ever anchor of 61% counts the YC deal as a seed, but this forecast counts only a financing above about $1M from outside investors that closes inside the window, so the anchor is cut to cover only rounds above $1M and only the share that close within 7 months (about 75 to 80 percent of eventual seed raisers close by month 14 to 20). Consumer payments is capital intensive and Apple Pay holds the iPhone tap to pay position, so I cut below the B2B anchor; the Fintech cohort median months to seed is 7, so only about half of eventual raisers close inside 7 months. Odds are not lifted for team or hot sector, per the winners test, and do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round of $1M to $3M, usually angels or a small seed fund. Fintech angels often write $1M to $3M for a payments founder with a regulated partner.

Institutional seed of $3M to $6M, the modal outcome in 2022 and later data (median $3.5M to $4.1M in round_benchmarks.csv, which mixes in the YC deal). The central case is a $3M to $6M seed from a fintech fund if a bank partner and a launch are in place.
Larger seed of $6M to $12M, where 42 percent of confirmed 2026 raises above $1M fell in the winners test. Large rounds need a viral launch or a distribution deal.
Upside band above $12M, reserved for a standout demo with a named lead. Needs NFC access and a clear user acquisition engine.

ladder.why_it_fails: Window of 7 months. The most likely miss is that a consumer wallet needs NFC access to the iPhone and a bank or card issuing partner, and Apple has long restricted third party tap to pay. Coin raised about $17M on hype and was sold for parts, Flinto and Cheqout raised little, so investors want a regulated partner and traction. Seven months is a short window, with almost no time for user data.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --industry B2B --years 2022-2024: series_a cond 33% (n=54), known-only 20%; months to series A median 30 (p25 22, p75 39).
anchors.adjustment_reason: The ever anchor is 33 percent, but only under a tenth of eventual Series A raisers have closed it by month 7 (p25 is 19 to 22 months from batch start), so the windowed value is much lower. Reaching a Series A in later years is common for companies with paying customers, but it falls outside this window.

bands.rationale: Thin or bridge style Series A below the 2022 and later median of $14M to $15M, the down or flat band.
Typical Series A near the 2022 and later quartiles ($11M to $21M raise).
Upside Series A led by a top tier fund once revenue is visible; current US medians are about $17M raise on $60M pre money.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A in 7 months would need real transaction volume and retention for a consumer wallet, and median time to Series A is about 28 months. Coin raised a Series A after a viral launch but could not ship a secure product in time, and Flinto merged away.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --industry B2B --years 2022-2024: series_b cond 17% (n=18); median months to series B 46 overall, 35.5 for 2022 and later (n=40).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Median time to a Series B is about three years from batch start, so inside a 7 month window almost only extreme outliers get there; windowed probability is far below the 17 percent ever anchor.

bands.rationale: Flat or small Series B, near the 2018 to 2021 median of $32M but with a lower valuation.
Typical Series B, in line with the 2022 and later median of about $40M.
Upside Series B for a category leader; 2022 and later posts reach $600M to $1B.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B inside 7 months would need enterprise revenue and a Series A first, and the median B2B path takes about three years from batch start (B2B median months to series B 47). Rescale, a simulation platform, took years of enterprise selling before its Series B. The likely failure is timing rather than a verdict on the idea.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only: series_c cond 36% (n=55) overall; B2B 2022-2024 cohort has 0 of 3 at Series C. Median months to series C about 61.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Series C normally lands about five years after the batch, so a window of 7 months makes it very unlikely; the ever anchor is cut to a token value.

bands.rationale: Typical Series C at the 2022 and later median of $74M.
Growth round for a scaled leader, near the 2022 and later p75 of $103M.
Upside round for a breakout company; only a few percent of YC companies get here.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C inside 7 months is almost outside the data: the median is about five years after batch start, and only 8 companies in the 2022 and later cohort have reached it. Failing here means the company has not scaled past a niche or the window closed first, not that the idea is bad.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most consumer wallets fail to get users to change a default payment habit, and platform control of NFC and big issuers make the market hard. Coin was sold for assets, Flinto merged into a scooter firm and Cheqout stalled; only wallets in underserved markets such as tpaga or Neema found a niche.

analogs.outcome_summary: Viral launch, about $17M raised, shipped late and Fitbit bought assets in 2016.

analogs.relevance: Phone based wallet and identity, Summer 2016.
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a $13.6M Series A in 2019 and $42M Series B in 2020 only after years in stealth, then sold to Oura.

analogs.relevance: Digital wallet for the underbanked in Mexico.
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised only a 1.5M pre seed after YC then merged in 2019.
Only the YC amount found and Square and Toast shipped similar features.

killers.risk: Apple restricts third party NFC and Apple Pay keeps the default position, so the wallet cannot match the tap experience.
killers.evidence: The CFPB found Apple bars third party apps from iPhone NFC tap to pay, though opening in some markets was announced later.
killers.mitigation: Launch on Android or in markets with open NFC and use online checkout first.

killers.risk: Consumer behaviour: users have no reason to switch from a wallet that is already on the phone.
killers.evidence: Apple Pay dominates US offline mobile payments per BCG, with PayPal losing share.
killers.mitigation: Pick a clear wedge such as a specific merchant group or rewards.

killers.risk: Regulation and card network partnerships take far longer than a seed runway.
killers.evidence: Payments companies need issuer and compliance partners; Proxy took three years in stealth before a Series A.
killers.mitigation: Partner with a licensed issuer from the start.

competition_now.name: Apple Pay
competition_now.what: Default wallet and the only tap to pay option on iOS in the US per the CFPB.

competition_now.name: Google Wallet and PayPal
competition_now.what: Android wallet and the online checkout leader.
competition_now.traction: PayPal remains leader in e-commerce payments per BCG.

competition_now.name: Status quo: physical cards and existing wallets
competition_now.what: Most consumers pay with cards already in Apple or Google Wallet.

technical_complexity.rationale: A wallet app is easy to prototype, but tap to pay, secure elements, card tokenization and fraud controls are hard, and a two person team depends on partners for each.

takeover_risk.rationale: Apple and Google already own the wallet and can add AI features at will; they have the distribution, so the risk is high unless the startup serves a niche.

evidence.claim: Apple Pay dominates US mobile wallet use, so a clear unmet need for a replacement is not evident.
Regulators have criticized Apple for blocking third party tap to pay, which creates an opening but not demand.

roadmap.goal: A working app that makes a real payment.
actions: Get a card issuing partner and complete a live transaction.
Define one customer group with a reason to switch.

roadmap.goal: Usage that supports a $3M to $6M seed.
actions: Sign one bank or merchant partner.
roadmap.proof: 1,000 active users and a partner agreement.

roadmap.goal: Volume and unit economics for a Series A.
roadmap.proof: Meaningful monthly payment volume with positive margin.

pros.point: Regulatory attention on Apple NFC restrictions may open the market.
pros.evidence: CFPB report criticized the wallet gatekeeping, and Apple opened NFC in some markets.

pros.point: Large payments market with room for niche entrants.
pros.evidence: BCG reports Apple Pay and PayPal share shifts.

brand.name: Uno Wallet
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Uno Wallet" --era 2022+: compound_words, flag 4+ syllables, cohort alive 95.3%, n=513
strengths: Simple words that are easy to understand
weaknesses: Collides with the card game Uno and says nothing distinctive
brand.rationale: Descriptive compound names such as Coin and Venmo can work in consumer finance, but Uno is a famous game brand and Wallet is generic, which weakens search and trademark options.

narrative.headline: A bold claim against a platform owner with no stated traction; 25 percent for a seed above $1M in 7 months.
narrative.general_summary: Uno Wallet wants to replace Apple Pay with an AI wallet. The need for a replacement is weak and Apple controls tap to pay on the iPhone, though regulators are pushing it open. Past wallets such as Coin and Flinto either raised hype money and faded or raised little. Over a window of only 7 months a seed above $1M is about a quarter, below the B2B anchor because of the consumer payments risk and the short time. A Series A in the window is very unlikely. The ladder does not rank this company above others. The main failure path is no reason for users to switch.

assumptions: No product detail beyond the one liner is known.
Blind forecast made as of 2026-04-06 for the window to 2026-11-17 (7 months). Seed means an outside round above about $1M closing in the window, not the standard YC deal of about $500K.
Coverage limit: 662 of 6,399 companies are researched, and the B2B 2022-2024 cohort has 107 companies, so cohort rates are wide.
Probabilities do not rank this company against others; the winners test found no separation between raisers and non-raisers.
